Metabolite Quality Control

quality_control.Rmd

The quality control pipeline can be implemented with the following lines of code, namely the metabolite_qc() function. You must specify the QC parameters in the slots of the Metabolomics object, this can either be done at object instantiation, or by later setting the slots.

This vignette walks through the key parameters and steps for performing QC using this function.

Creating a Metabolites Object

Before performing QC, you need a Metabolites object, which contains metabolomics data along with metadata.

library(metaboprep2)

# Example Metabolon (format 1) raw data file
filepath <- system.file("extdata", "metabolon_v1_example.xlsx", package = "metaboprep2")

# Create a Metabolites object with the desired parameters
metabolites <- Metabolites(project_name              = "ExampleProject", 
                           filepath                  = filepath,
                           format                    = "metabolon_v1",   
                           feature_missingness       = 0.2,
                           sample_missingness        = 0.2,
                           total_peak_area_sd        = 5,
                           outlier_udist             = 5,
                           outlier_treatment         = "leave_be",
                           winsorize_quantile        = 1,
                           tree_cut_height           = 0.5,
                           pc_outlier_sd             = 5,
                           derived_var_exclusion     = TRUE,
                           xenobiotics_var_exclusion = TRUE)

# Import the data 
metabolites <- import_data(metabolites)
#> Using cached MetaboAnalyst DB.
#> Attempting join [features$hmdb] ~ [annotation$hmdb_id] 
#> Attempting join [features$kegg] ~ [annotation$kegg_id] 
#> Attempting join [features$metabolite_id] ~ [annotation$name] 
#> Attempting join [features$comp_id] ~ [annotation$comp_id]
#> Warning in annotate_features(features, fixed_match_cols = list(hmdb_id = "hmdb", : 100 unannotated metabolites remain after merging with metabolomics database

Performing Metabolite Quality Control

The metabolite_qc() function applies multiple QC filters based on missingness, outlier detection, PCA-based QC. This generates another layer to the data matrices named post_qc. And intermediate qcing layer is also generated.

metabolites <- metabolite_qc(metabolites, source = "raw")
#> 
#> ── Starting Metabolite QC Process ──────────────────────────────────────────────

#> ℹ Sample & Feature Summary Statistics for raw data...

Figures

Currently the feature tree object is stored in the metabolites object @feature_tree slot.

plot(get_feature_tree(metabolites, layer="post_qc"))
